Mechanics are everything: if you fail a mechanic, the boss gets stronger. In a weak team, failing twice can make the boss impossible, too risky or too expensive to kill in time.

Use {item:Stone Skin Amulet|Stone Skin Amulets} and {item:Might Ring|Might Rings} throughout the **whole** fight, especially the shooters: the {creature:Dreadful Harvester|Dreadful Harvesters} hit very hard and deal critical hits.
Shooters: always stay alert and move away from melee hits. All the bosses have summons that hit hard, so drag them (lure) to the Knight whenever possible.

Because of the taints, Dreadful Harvesters keep appearing and teleporting. Since the behaviour of the taints is known (not random), each player's position, the way they move and the attacks they choose control how many appear and where they go. For lower-level teams, positioning is a mechanic in itself.
Before each boss, agree on everyone's roles (who steps on what, who does each mechanic and in what order).
1. Before you start: how the quest works
Soul War is mostly a sequence of bosses, similar to the {wiki:Feaster of Souls Quest}: five access bosses, each at the end of an area with its own challenge, and a final boss.

All the bosses, including the final one, accept teams of **up to 5 players**. The five access bosses have a **20-hour** cooldown; the final boss, {creature:Goshnar's Megalomania}, has **68 hours** (2 days and 20 hours). {creature:Goshnar's Malice}, {creature:Goshnar's Greed}, {creature:Goshnar's Spite}, {creature:Goshnar's Cruelty} and {creature:Goshnar's Megalomania} give you at most **20 minutes** of fighting.

Each area has an access challenge (raids, kills, energies, shrines). That access progress **is lost if you leave the area**: to get back to the boss you would have to repeat the access from the start.
Do not leave the area halfway through the access, not even by mistake (exit teleports, wrong portals).
The final boss always requires all five
Unlike most quests, **every time** you want to kill {creature:Goshnar's Megalomania} you must first kill the five access bosses. This applies to the first time and to every repeat.

You can kill the bosses in any order you like: the taints always come to you in the same order. However, because of the difficulty of the accesses and the bosses, most players use this order (it is the order of this guide):
Taints you take into the fight
2. Reaching Zarganash and the Soul War hub
The hub is inside {wiki:Zarganash}, the area you opened in the {wiki:Feaster of Souls Quest}. The entrance is an invisible teleport in {wiki:Vengoth}.

First get to **Yalahar** by boat ({key:hi}, {key:yalahar}, {key:yes}): from Thais with {npc:Captain Bluebear} (200 gp), from Carlin with {npc:Captain Greyhound} (185 gp), from Darashia with {npc:Petros} (210 gp), from Ankrahmun with {npc:Captain Sinbeard} (230 gp) or from Liberty Bay with **Jack Fate** (275 gp). There is no direct boat to Yalahar from Venore or Edron. In Yalahar, go to the **Trade Quarter** docks (straight **south** from the main gate) and talk to {npc:Harlow}: {key:hi}, {key:vengoth}, {key:yes} (100 gp). He drops you off in the **west** of {wiki:Vengoth}.

From where Harlow drops you off, walk **north-east** to the invisible teleport to {wiki:Zarganash}, at the coordinate spot, and step into it. Zarganash is a hunting place for level 300+, with {creature:Flimsy Lost Soul|Flimsy}, {creature:Mean Lost Soul|Mean} and {creature:Freakish Lost Soul|Freakish Lost Souls}.
Inside Zarganash, cross the dungeon to the far **south-west** and step into the teleport there. You end up in a teleport hub: the Soul War hub.
South-west teleport to the Soul War hub
Map of Zarganash (from the Feaster of Souls Quest), to find your way around inside
In the hub, talk to the {npc:Flickering Soul} (Goshnar's soul): {key:hi}, {key:task} and {key:yes}. You now have to destroy Goshnar's *fettered vices*.

In the hub there is a row of **Fog Portals**, each leading to an area with a challenge you must complete to reach that area's boss. Counting from **left to right**: 1st {wiki:Claustrophobic Inferno} ({creature:Goshnar's Malice}), 2nd {wiki:Rotten Wasteland} ({creature:Goshnar's Hatred}), 3rd (the middle one) {wiki:Ebb and Flow} ({creature:Goshnar's Spite}), 4th {wiki:Furious Crater} ({creature:Goshnar's Cruelty}) and 5th (the rightmost one) {wiki:Mirrored Nightmare} ({creature:Goshnar's Greed}). The final boss portal is in the **south-west** of the hub and the reward room portal is behind a {npc:Flickering Soul}, in the main room.
The hub's Fog Portals and each area's boss
Each portal first takes you to a **safe zone** inside the hunting area: get ready there before moving on.

The only exit the wiki describes is the {wiki:Magic Forcefield} in the reward room (section 15), which takes you to the **Thais depot**, but you only use it after the final boss. The wiki does not describe the way back from the hub to Zarganash: go back the way you came in (the south-west teleport and then through Zarganash to the invisible teleport in Vengoth). In Vengoth, walk **south-west** to {npc:Harlow} and say {key:hi}, {key:yalahar}, {key:yes} (50 gp) to return to Yalahar's Trade Quarter.
If you cannot find the exit, a {item:Temple Teleport Scroll} sends you to your town's temple (it does not work in No-Logout zones or with a Logout Block or Protection Zone Block).

Before you kill the first boss, make sure you understand {wiki:Goshnar's Taints|Goshnar's Taints}. They are special conditions you gain by killing the access bosses: they give penalties (from 1 to 5) but also rewards (more experience and the chance of looting {item:Bag You Desire|Bags You Desire}). They only work inside the Soul War areas, including the boss rooms; outside them they do nothing.

You gain one taint for each access boss you kill. The taints **always come in the same order**, whatever the boss. Killing the same boss several times does **not** give a new taint: to have all five you must kill the five bosses. If you die during the fight but have dealt damage to the boss, you still receive the taint, as long as the team finishes it off (the same applies to the final boss and to completing the quest). You can see your taints in the **Status Bar**; to find out which bosses you have them from, say {key:shards} to the {npc:Flickering Soul}.
These are the five penalties, in the order you receive them:
Penalty (only in the Soul War areas)
10% chance of a creature teleporting next to you
0.5% chance of a new creature appearing near you when you hit another creature
10% chance for a creature to fully heal instead of dying
You lose 10% of your current health and mana every 10 seconds

In each zone there is one creature with this ability, and each one makes a sound before teleporting (table). Every 2 seconds they check whether a player with this taint is in range and teleport to the **farthest** player within range (who may even be off your screen). That player gets an invisible 10-second cooldown: if another creature tries to teleport to them during that time, the teleport is cancelled. That is why the Paladin usually stays far from the Knight's box, so that he is the target. Two seconds before the teleport a warning appears on the creature and on the target: a Death Effect in the hunting zones and a Purple Electricity Effect in the boss fights.
{creature:Dreadful Harvester} (with the 1st taint also the {creature:Spiteful Spitter|Spiteful Spitters})

If you react quickly to the Death Effect and put a {item:Magic Wall Rune} on the sqm where the target was when the effect appeared, the teleport is cancelled. Creatures only teleport to places they could reach on foot: if you close the doors or put Magic Walls in the house entrances in the Mirrored Nightmare **before** the warning, they appear at the nearest reachable spot, outside the house (they can also land on stairs and change floor).

Hitting any creature in the Soul War zones can make another one appear (always the same creature as for the 1st taint, with the sound from the table above). Field damage and damage over time (such as burning) do not count. There is a 30-second cooldown per character; if the creature that triggered the taint dies before the new one appears, the new one does not appear. A Teleport Effect warns you 3 seconds before, but this spawn **cannot** be prevented (not even with Magic Wall). The new creature has the same health, experience and loot as the normal ones and disappears after 10 minutes if you do not kill it (20 seconds before, it says *My time is ticking away.*).

**3rd:** all damage you take in the Soul War zones increases by 15%. **4th:** any creature in the zones (and the Dreadful Harvesters in the boss fights) has a 10% chance to fully heal on the blow that would have killed it, with the orange message *Health restored by the mystic powers of Zarganash!* — there is no way to prevent it. **5th:** you lose 10% of your **current** health and mana every 10 seconds. Nothing reduces this loss ({spell:Magic Shield} and {item:Energy Ring} do not prevent the health loss) and it does not even show up as damage on screen. In practice, you cannot keep much more mana than 10 times what your best mana potion restores.
The 5th taint is applied in the final boss room: you go in with full mana and it drops very quickly. This is normal, do not panic.

The normal way is to kill the final boss, {creature:Goshnar's Megalomania}: the taints of the whole team disappear (anyone who dies in the fight is also cleansed if they dealt damage to the boss). If the team **fails** the final boss, each player loses their last two taints and the progress of **two random bosses** (the same for the whole party): you can see which ones you have to repeat by saying {key:shards} to the {npc:Flickering Soul}. You can also clear the taints by saying {key:penalties} or {key:taints}, but only two weeks after the last time you gained or lost a taint (killing the same boss again does not count).
Taint advantages: Bag You Desire and Goshnar's Tribute

With at least one taint, creatures in the Soul War zones can drop a {item:Bag You Desire} (without taints only the bosses can give it). More taints, higher chance; killing the same boss several times does not increase the chance. The bag always drops inside a Reward Container and each party member has their own chance, based on their taints. At {creature:Goshnar's Megalomania}, each kill without the bag slightly increases the next chance, which resets when it drops. In addition, with **Goshnar's Tribute**, if all party members have at least one taint, the party gets more experience and a chance of a second loot; the member with the **fewest** taints is what counts (if one has zero, nobody gets the bonus).
The second loot only applies to normal loot, not to the Bag You Desire. In the Highscores, each kill of an access boss is worth 1 point and each kill of Goshnar's Megalomania is worth 10.
4. Claustrophobic Inferno — surviving the three raids
**Recommended protection:** Death and Fire. **Element to use:** Ice. You have to survive three raids in a row, 2 minutes each, in an enclosed zone.
In the hub, enter the **1st Fog Portal from the left**. You arrive at the safe zone of the {wiki:Claustrophobic Inferno}.

Enter the raid zone **all together**: the first player to pass the {item:Sandtimer} at the entrance starts the timer and, seconds later, a wall appears that blocks the entrance. Shortly afterwards several waves of {creature:Brachiodemon|Brachiodemons} and {creature:Infernal Phantom|Infernal Phantoms} start to appear. You have to **survive 2 minutes**; at the end, the remaining monsters disappear and the team is teleported to the next area.
Anyone left behind is shut outside the wall.

Run to a corner: the shooters up against the walls and the Knight a few steps into the spawn, so the creatures pick him as their target when they appear. Constant damage is the most important thing: the most common cause of failure is not killing the creatures quickly, which lets the leftover ones go after the shooters. Also watch out for the {creature:Infernal Demon|Infernal Demons}: they always attack the character with the **lowest maximum health**.
After each raid: go down the stairs
At the end of each raid you are teleported right next to a {wiki:Magic Forcefield|teleport}: that teleport is the **exit**. To continue, always follow the nearby **stairs** downwards.
Do not enter the teleport next to the arrival point if you want to continue: you leave the zone and lose your access progress.
In the first raid, the box is usually made at the marked spot.
Go down the stairs and repeat in the second raid (slightly different layout). The box is usually made here.
Go down again and do the third raid. After it, the team is sent to a room with a **Fog Portal** that leads to the lever room of {creature:Goshnar's Malice}.
After leaving a raid area, each player has a 3-minute cooldown before they can enter that area again.

The {wiki:Magic Forcefield|teleport} that appears next to the spot where you are teleported at the end of each raid is the zone's **exit** (the wiki does not say where it takes you). Before the first raid, go back through the Fog Portal you came in by. Remember that leaving erases your access progress: next time you repeat all three raids.
**Recommended protection:** Death (and Ice only for the Knight, because of Malice's wave and beam). The boss has 550 000 health, heals when it hits you and reflects 100% of the damage it takes.

After the third raid, the Fog Portal in the final room takes you to the **lever room** of {creature:Goshnar's Malice}: the team (up to 5 players) enters the fight through that room's lever. You have at most **20 minutes** of fighting and the boss has a **20-hour** cooldown.

Right at the start, the Knight has to hold all the creatures: {creature:Goshnar's Malice}, two {creature:Dreadful Harvester|Dreadful Harvesters} and two {creature:Malicious Soul|Malicious Souls}. Not all of them appear straight away; some show up after a few seconds.
Use {spell:Challenge} as much as possible: the boss and the summons switch targets often.

Malice **heals when it deals damage**, so avoid being hit by its spells. And it **reflects 100%** of the damage it takes: the shooters' {item:Stone Skin Amulet|Stone Skin Amulets} and {item:Might Ring|Might Rings} get used up even without being attacked directly, so swap them constantly. Anyone dealing physical or death damage with their weapon loses **two charges** of Stone Skin per turn.

When the message *GOSHNAR'S MALICE PREPARES TO DEVOUR A TRAPPED SOUL!* appears, a {creature:Soul Cage} immediately shows up in the **north** part of the room. All the shooters attack it to kill it as fast as possible: you have **14 seconds**. If you fail, Malice absorbs it (*GOSHNAR'S MALICE DEVOURS THE SOUL AND BECAME HARDER TO DEFEAT!*) and gets stronger: it takes less damage, deals more and its reflection goes up (on the first failure, from 100% to about 200%). The Soul Cage itself also reflects a small part of the damage of all elements.

Failing a single Soul Cage can be enough for the boss to become too strong for you to kill in time. Do not leave Malice next to the Soul Cage: it can heal itself and its summons for 14 000 to 20 000 health.

When *A MALICIOUS SOUL FLOOD IS IMMINENT!* appears, several white tiles show up around the room (not always in the same places). **3 seconds** later, all the floor that has **not** changed is hit by a Red Smoke Effect that deals about 7 000 to 9 000 death damage: stand on a white tile.
White tile (White Stone Tile): stand on it

The Knight has to keep moving so as not to stand in front of the boss and to reach the white tiles. Alternative: the Knight stands against a wall and lets himself be surrounded by the boss and the 4 summons. He should only do this when he is sure the boss is **diagonal** to him; otherwise he takes the waves the whole time, suffers a lot of damage and heals the boss through Life Leech. This strategy makes the fight more static, but demands close attention to the white tiles (so the Knight does not get hit by the explosion) and care when setting up the box so the boss ends up diagonal.

You can also simply tank the tile explosion with a {item:Stone Skin Amulet}, a {item:Might Ring} and at least one piece with the {wiki:Powerful Lich Shroud|Powerful Lich Shroud} imbuement: you take about 1 000 to 1 200 damage. That way everyone can focus on the Soul Cage (if it appears at the same time) and the Druids always stay in range to heal the Knight.
If you choose to tank the explosion, watch your Stone Skin charges: the reflection can use it up even before the explosion.
Keep attacking the boss while you deal with the two mechanics until it dies. You get your first taint (section 3).
After the boss: back to the hub

The wiki does not describe how to leave the {creature:Goshnar's Malice} room or the way back to the hub. Go back the way you came; if there is no passage, a {item:Temple Teleport Scroll} sends you to your city's temple (it does not work in No-Logout zones or with a Logout Block or Protection Zone Block), and return to the hub via the route in section 2. In the recommended order, the next zone is the {wiki:Mirrored Nightmare} (the rightmost Fog Portal).
**Recommended protection:** Holy and Ice. **Element to use:** Fire. The map of this zone is a nightmare version of the city of Thais.
In the hub, enter the **rightmost** Fog Portal (5th from the left). You arrive at the safe zone of the {wiki:Mirrored Nightmare}.

There are several wall mirrors you can click on: the mirror breaks and a {creature:Mirror Image} appears. When you attack a Mirror Image, it turns into an Apparition. It is more likely to turn into the Apparition of the vocation of whoever attacked it first, but any other may come out. There are more Mirror Images in the **underground** part of the map, but there is less space there, which makes it more dangerous.
Keep the kills of each vocation balanced (whoever attacks first influences the vocation) so you do not waste time on Apparitions you no longer need.
To enter the boss room you have to kill **25 Apparitions of each vocation**:
With 25 kills of each, go to the **temple portal** (see map) to reach {creature:Goshnar's Greed}.
Mirrored Nightmare: location of the portal in the temple
The wiki does not describe the exit from this zone: go back to the safe zone you came in through. Remember that leaving erases your kill progress.
Greed starts out immune to all damage. It only becomes vulnerable after you kill 5 Greedbeasts, and even then only for 40 seconds at a time.

The temple portal in the {wiki:Mirrored Nightmare} (section 6) takes you to {creature:Goshnar's Greed}. The team can have up to 5 players; you have at most **20 minutes** of fighting and the boss has a **20-hour** cooldown.

Since the shooters handle the mechanics, the Knight is free to block {creature:Goshnar's Greed} in the **north** of the room. There is no point attacking it while it is invulnerable: the Knight can walk left and right to reduce the damage taken and stop it from healing with Life Leech.

A {creature:Greedbeast} appears in the **centre-left** part of the room. Kill it as fast as possible: only after **5 Greedbeasts are dead** does the boss become vulnerable (each kill gives *The death of the greedbeast increases the need of Goshnar's Greed to feed!*). Shooters can use {item:Sudden Death Rune|Sudden Death Runes}, but waves also work well. Killing a Greedbeast while the boss is already vulnerable **does not count** towards the next round.
The Greedbeast deals a lot of Life Drain damage: ideally a Paladin blocks it with a {item:Necklace of the Deep}.

In this phase the boss is stuck in the **north-west** of the room and vulnerable for **40 seconds**. A {creature:Soul Sphere} appears in the **north-east** and moves slowly towards the boss: if it gets there, it **heals it completely**. A common strategy is for one shooter to kill the Soul Sphere while the others deal as much damage as possible to the boss; when the sphere dies, that shooter also attacks the boss.

Two {creature:Weak Soul|Weak Souls} (one on the left and one on the right) and a {creature:Soulsnatcher} (to the south) appear. You have to lure them onto one of the **blue vortices** ({item:Active Spirit Vortex}) scattered around the room so they disappear. The vortices alternate: 15 seconds active (blue vortex) and 25 seconds inactive (crystal, {item:Inactive Vortex}). A Weak Soul that does not leave within 8 seconds becomes a {creature:Strong Soul} and, 8 seconds later, a {creature:Powerful Soul}; if the Powerful Soul is not dealt with within 8 seconds, it disappears and **strengthens the boss**.

During the vulnerable phase a Greedbeast keeps appearing. Leave it on low health and only kill it **after** the boss becomes invulnerable again: that way you immediately get one of the 5 kills for the next round. Being slow with the Greedbeasts, or killing them while the boss is vulnerable, costs you time and can make a lower-level team run out of time.

It is common to put the 4 shooters in a line across the middle of the room, each with a task: one at the far **left**, the Paladin right **above** the spot where the Greedbeast appears, another in the **centre** to deal with the Soulsnatcher and the last one at the far **right**. Use {item:Magic Wall Rune|Magic Walls} and {item:Wild Growth Rune|Wild Growths} to steer the Weak Souls to the vortices at the edge of the room.
Repeat these mechanics until the boss dies: damage in the vulnerable phase is critical, because it is short.
2nd Goshnar's Taint; 150 000 experience; boss loot (see section 15)
After the boss: back to the hub

The wiki does not describe how to leave the {creature:Goshnar's Greed} room or the way back to the hub. Go back the way you came; if there is no passage, a {item:Temple Teleport Scroll} sends you to your city's temple (it does not work in No-Logout zones or with a Logout Block or Protection Zone Block), and return to the hub via the route in section 2. In the recommended order, the next zone is {wiki:Ebb and Flow} (the middle Fog Portal).
8. Ebb and Flow — hunting the Hazardous Phantoms

**Recommended protection:** Earth and Ice. **Element to use:** Fire. This is the longest access of the quest (it can take over 1 hour). Three of the four creatures in the zone (all except the {creature:Turbulent Elemental|Turbulent Elementals}) cause **Fear**: a Ghost Smoke Effect announces the Fear and, 2 seconds later, a blue ghost applies it to a character. With Fear, you run away from the creatures for 3 seconds without being able to stop or use spells (runes and potions work).
Learn to recognise the two effects: first the smoke, then the blue ghost that applies the Fear.
Warning: Fear is about to be applied
Blue ghost: Fear is applied to a character
Bombs on the floor (for example {item:Fire Bomb Rune|Fire Bombs}) stop your character from walking over them while you are under Fear.

In the hub, enter the **middle** Fog Portal (3rd from the left). You arrive at the safe zone of {wiki:Ebb and Flow}. To reach the boss you have to kill **20 {creature:Hazardous Phantom|Hazardous Phantoms}**. The catch: the map alternates between **flooded** and **dry** every **2 minutes**.
Ebb and Flow (location on the map)

With water, you are on the **rooftops** of the buildings and can cross from one building to another via the **rafts** between them. You cannot use the buildings' ramps to go down to the floor below (outside the buildings). If you fall through one of the **holes**, you end up on the floor below **inside** the building, with no way to get back up and unable to leave through the doors (they do not open). If you are on a raft when the water goes down, you fall to the floor below (outside the buildings).
The holes only work one way. Beware of Fear near them: you can be thrown down there or onto another island across several rafts.

Without water, you walk freely on the floor below, open doors, go into and around the buildings and use the ramps to go up or down, but you **cannot** use the rafts to jump between rooftops. If you are **not** on a raft when the water rises, you are teleported to the entrance (safe zone); if you are on a raft, you go to the rooftop of the nearest building.
Since September 2022 it is no longer possible to use {spell:Levitate} from the floor below onto the rafts. Videos or guides that suggest this predate that change.

There is a visual cue: small puddles of water on the ground change from small to medium **80 seconds** after the map dries, which means you have 40 more seconds in the dry. Since this is hard to notice while fighting, it is best to use an **external 2-minute looping timer**, synced with the water.
The puddles that change size 80 s after the map dries
Safe strategy: run to the south-east raft

Wait for the last **20 to 30 seconds** before the water rises and run with the whole team to the **south-east raft**. If someone gets stuck or is thrown by Fear and does not reach the raft, they only need to survive a few seconds until the water rises and teleports them to the safe zone (as long as they are not on a raft). On the raft, put down {item:Fire Bomb Rune|Fire Bombs} and stand on them so you are not thrown by Fear, and fend off the creatures that followed you for the remaining seconds. When the water rises, whoever is on the raft goes to the building to its **west**: stay in a corner and throw Fire Bombs around the building so you are not thrown into the holes or across the rafts to other buildings.
This strategy is dangerous and requires very good timing; if it fails, the team stays too long on the floor below and has a hard time when the water rises.

Stronger teams can run as soon as the water goes down and clear the monsters before the south-east raft, at the marked spot. Only do this if the team can handle all the monsters in the area (enough to surround the Knight and several more). The advantage is that there is time left to recover mana and prepare for the water rising.
Spot to clear before the south-east raft

In the **south** building, keep killing the creatures that keep appearing around you, among them a {creature:Hazardous Phantom}, until you reach **20** kills. Hazardous Phantoms can take a few minutes to appear. Stronger or more experienced teams can clear other boxes and get Hazardous from several places: for example, going down the stairs to the **south-east** of this building there is another Hazardous right to the **south**, which almost doubles the speed.
Second Hazardous Phantom (to the south, after the south-east stairs)
With the second Hazardous you risk having a full spawn on both floors and being thrown west by Fear, where there are lots of monsters.
With the 20 kills you gain access to the {creature:Goshnar's Spite} room. The wiki does not say where the boss portal is in this zone: use the zone maps.

If the water rises while you are on the floor below and not on a raft, you are teleported to the safe zone at the entrance. To leave the buildings you have to use the doors, which is only possible with the water down. Remember that leaving the zone erases your kill progress.
**Recommended protection:** Death, Earth and Energy. **Elements to use:** Death and Fire. It is one of the easiest bosses of the quest (which is why it is the recommended 3rd), but it can cause Fear.

With the 20 {creature:Hazardous Phantom} kills done in {wiki:Ebb and Flow} (section 8), the team (up to 5 players) enters the {creature:Goshnar's Spite} room. You have at most **20 minutes** of fighting and the boss has a **20-hour** cooldown.

Every **14 seconds** a purple flame ({item:Cleansed Soul Splinter}) appears on one side of the room (*A soulfire is blazing! Stomp it out in time!*). A player has to step on it to make it disappear (*The soul fire was stomped out in time! Your soul will now have to recover before you can do this again.*). After that, that player cannot put out flames for **60 seconds** (*Your soul has recovered!*). That is why **all** players, including the Knight, take turns stepping on the flames, in a fixed order agreed beforehand. If nobody steps on it, the flame disappears after a few seconds and the boss gets stronger (*Goshnar's Spite absorbs the soulfire!*).

When you kill a {creature:Weeping Soul}, its body stays on the ground as a {item:Pool of Tears}. Anyone who steps in a pool is transformed into a {creature:Water Elemental} (*You are soaked by tears of the weeping soul!*) and starts taking **huge** energy damage from the energy attacks of the boss and the summons. Since you will not always manage to avoid them, use some energy protection.

Besides the boss there are the usual {creature:Dreadful Harvester|Dreadful Harvesters}, {creature:Weeping Soul|Weeping Souls} and {creature:Spiteful Spitter|Spiteful Spitters}. The Knight blocks the boss in the **centre** of the room; the shooters move around to lure the summons to the Knight and avoid the melee hits. If there are too many summons alive at the same time, use area attacks (waves and {item:Great Fireball Rune|Great Fireball Runes}). The mages attack {creature:Goshnar's Spite} with spells and {item:Sudden Death Rune|Sudden Death Runes}.

In the recommended order, the team has **2 taints** in this fight: controlling the number of summons in the room becomes crucial because of the extra Dreadful Harvesters, and can make the difference between winning and losing. The fight is simple, but communication is essential: everyone has to know who steps on the next flame and where it appeared.
It is common to put {item:Fire Bomb Rune|Fire Bombs} on the floor in the centre, where the Knight blocks the boss, so he does not run off when he gets Fear.
With the Fire Bombs, the Knight is very vulnerable while the Fear lasts.
Keep the flames out and the summons under control until the boss dies.
After the boss: back to the hub

The wiki does not describe how to leave the {creature:Goshnar's Spite} room or the way back to the hub. Go back the way you came; if there is no passage, a {item:Temple Teleport Scroll} sends you to your city's temple (it does not work in No-Logout zones or with a Logout Block or Protection Zone Block), and return to the hub via the route in section 2. In the recommended order, the next zone is the {wiki:Furious Crater} (4th Fog Portal from the left).

**Recommended protection:** Holy and Energy. **Element to use:** Earth. The {wiki:Furious Crater} is a hollow rock south of Kilmaresh and east of Oramond, which can only be reached through the hub teleport. It has 5 floors: 3 are the hunting zones, the 4th has the lever that leads to the floor below, where {creature:Goshnar's Cruelty} is.
In the hub, enter the **4th Fog Portal from the left**. You arrive at the safe zone of the Furious Crater.

To go down a floor you have to collect **40**, **55** and **70** {item:Pulsating Energy|Pulsating Energies}, on the 1st, 2nd and 3rd floors respectively. The energies work like creature blood: hit the creatures until they leave energies on the ground and then **walk over** them. Follow your progress in the **Quest Log**.
Each player has to collect their own energies: only go down when everyone is charged.
Beware of the Cloaks of Terror's blood

When you hit a {creature:Cloak of Terror}, a pool of {item:The Blood of Cloak of Terror} appears beneath it. It works like an energy field, but deals much more damage to whoever steps on it, depending on your total health and the size of the pool (large, medium or small): up to about 20% of your maximum health. And Cloaks of Terror heal 1 500 to 2 000 health when they walk over their own blood.

Enter the respawn and lure one or two {creature:Vibrant Phantom|Vibrant Phantoms} and/or {creature:Courage Leech|Courage Leeches}. Put {item:Fire Bomb Rune|Fire Bombs} or {item:Poison Bomb Rune|Poison Bombs} on the ground and make them walk over them: those hits are enough for them to drop several energies. If a Cloak of Terror appears, lure it away, or stop running so you do not spread the blood and kill it with single-target attacks. When everyone is charged, go down through the **Fog teleporter** on the **east** side of the area.

On arriving at this floor you immediately face several monsters (from a little under a box to more than a box, depending on the respawn). Put all the melee monsters on the Knight and do not use {spell:Chivalrous Challenge} on the Vibrant Phantoms before the Cloaks and most of the Courages are dead. With the area secured, repeat the bomb strategy with the Phantoms and the Courages. Depending on the team's strength, the respawn may come back before everyone has finished. When everyone is charged, go down through the **Fog teleporter right next to the entrance** of this floor.

Once again, you may have several monsters right at the entrance. Repeat the strategy until the whole team is charged; since more energies are needed here, the respawn will almost certainly come back before you finish. With everyone charged, enter the **lever room** through the **Fog teleporter right next to the entrance**.

More experienced players send the Paladin to jump down first to the 2nd and 3rd floors and lure most of the monsters away from the entrance. Since all the floors are circular, he can go all the way round to the entrance or turn back after taking them to the other side.

The wiki does not describe the exit from the zone: go back to the safe zone you came in through. Remember that leaving erases the collected energies (you have to repeat the access every time you enter).

**Recommended protection:** Death and Fire. With **3 taints**, this is one of the hardest parts of the quest. The longer the fight lasts, the more resistant the boss becomes. Define each player's role clearly beforehand and memorise where each creature appears.

The Fog teleporter on the 3rd floor of the {wiki:Furious Crater} takes you to the **lever room** (4th floor of the crater). The lever takes the team (up to 5 players) to the floor below, where {creature:Goshnar's Cruelty} is. You have at most **20 minutes** of fighting and the boss has a **20-hour** cooldown.
Mechanic: Poor Souls and A Greedy Eye

{creature:Poor Soul|Poor Souls} appear in the **south-west** part of the room. One shooter stays near that spot to become their target and lures them to the **north** of the room, in front of {creature:A Greedy Eye}. When the Greedy Eye's beam hits the Poor Soul, it dies and leaves a {item:Some Mortal Essence} on the ground.
The Greedy Eye's beam also hits you: 3 000 drown damage (Drown).

Take the Mortal Essence to the **south** of the room and use it on the {item:Greedy Maw}. When it works, *The hunger for cruelty has lessened!* appears. The mechanic has a cooldown (or a limit): if it sometimes does not work, it means you are doing it faster than is possible, which is a good sign.
The boss's growing resistance cannot be avoided, but these two mechanics slow it down considerably.
Every 60 to 70 seconds *Goshnar's Cruelty begins to channel its energy! Prepare!* appears and, 6 seconds later, an explosion hits the whole room and deals up to 3 000 physical damage to everyone.

Every 30 seconds, a random player is transformed into a {creature:Massive Fire Elemental} and explodes 6 seconds later, taking and dealing up to 3 500 fire damage in a huge area around them. If it is you, move away from the others.
Massive Fire Elemental: move away from the team before you explode
A {creature:Mean Maw} also appears in the **centre-south** part of the room. It is immune to {spell:Challenge}: the only way for the Knight to become its target is to block its path while it walks.

The Knight stays near the **centre**, so the boss can be attacked from all sides and so he is close to the Mean Maw's spot when it appears. If the Mean Maw goes after a shooter, getting it back to the Knight is hard for an inexperienced team and risks losing the aggro of the boss and the summons. Two shooters (usually the Paladin and the Sorcerer) handle the Poor Souls and the Mortal Essences, on the **left** side; the other two stay by the **right** wall or to the **south**, just dealing damage and healing. They can swap roles: for example, if the Poor Souls mage runs out of mana, they swap with another shooter. Balance single-target attacks on the boss with area damage to clear the summons.

Some teams start the fight straight away with the {wiki:Avatar|Avatar} spells, to deal maximum damage while the boss has less resistance. Lower-level teams can save them for moments with too many summons, which are much easier to clear in Avatar form.
Deal as much damage as possible while you do the mechanics: this is a very time-sensitive fight.
After the boss: back to the hub

The wiki does not describe how to leave the {creature:Goshnar's Cruelty} room or the way back to the hub. Go back the way you came; if there is no passage, a {item:Temple Teleport Scroll} sends you to your city's temple (it does not work in No-Logout zones or with a Logout Block or Protection Zone Block), and return to the hub via the route in section 2. In the recommended order, the next zone is the {wiki:Rotten Wasteland} (2nd Fog Portal from the left).
**Recommended protection:** Holy and Earth. **Element to use:** Fire. The creatures in this zone cause **Rooted**: you are stuck in place for 3 seconds, unable to move.

In the hub, enter the **2nd Fog Portal from the left**. You arrive at the safe zone of the {wiki:Rotten Wasteland}; when you enter the respawn you are in the **main hall**. To reach the boss you have to activate a portal using **four shrines**, in four branches spread over three floors. You can see in the **Quest Log** which shrines you have already activated.

The routes are straightforward (see the maps in the following steps). When you reach the shrine (the **orange star** on the map), **all** players in the team have to use it to gain access. Then enter the teleport next to the shrine (the **blue flag** on the map): it takes you back to the centre of the main hall, which is not a safe zone but is very close to it.
Anyone who does not use the shrine does not get access.
Follow the **south-east** branch from the main hall to the {item:Shrine (Blue)}, use it (the whole team) and go back through the teleport next to it.
Follow the **north-west** branch to the {item:Shrine (Green)}, use it and go back through the teleport next to it.
Follow the **north-east** branch to the {item:Shrine (Orange)}, use it and go back through the teleport next to it.
Follow the **south-west** branch to the {item:Shrine (Violet)}, use it and go back through the teleport next to it.
With the four shrines activated, go to the far **west** of the main hall, go through the door and down the stairs. There you will find the portal to the lever room of {creature:Goshnar's Hatred}.

The wiki does not describe the exit from the zone: go back to the safe zone you came in through (it is near the centre of the main hall, where the shrine teleports drop you off). Remember that leaving erases the activated shrines.
**Recommended protection:** Death and Fire. It is one of the easiest bosses, which is why it comes 5th, when you already have **4 taints**.

The portal at the far end of the {wiki:Rotten Wasteland} (section 12) takes you to the **lever room** of {creature:Goshnar's Hatred}: the team (up to 5 players) enters the fight through the lever. The boss has a **20-hour** cooldown.

In the centre of the room there is a bonfire that keeps growing: {item:Ashes of Burning Hatred}, {item:Spark of Burning Hatred}, {item:Flame of Burning Hatred} and {item:Blaze of Burning Hatred}. If the flame grows, {creature:Goshnar's Hatred} gets stronger. To prevent this, kill the {creature:Hateful Soul|Hateful Souls} in the room and use their bodies ({item:Sorrow}) on the bonfire, as often as possible.

Each character has an individual counter: an icon next to their name, below the Party or Guild icon, that looks like a little piece of paper with a battle sign. It starts at zero and goes up by 1 every 3 seconds. When it reaches **30**, the character takes a heavy hit of death damage every 3 seconds (*The dread's torment is killing you!*). To reset it, destroy the {creature:Symbol of Hatred|Symbols of Hatred} that appear to the **east** and **west** of the room and step on their remains ({item:Condensed Remorse}).

Throughout the fight, every 8 seconds there is an exori-like energy spell around each character. Despite the energy animation, it deals Life Drain damage to anyone in the area: do not stand right next to each other.

The team keeps moving between the **two pillars**, attacking the pillar, the boss and the Hateful Souls at the same time with area damage. The shooters preferably stay to the **north** and **south** of the room and leave the middle free for the Knight, except whoever is handling the Burning Hatred. At the same time, take turns in an agreed order to reset the Dread, so nobody takes the heavy death hits.
Keep the bonfire small and the counters low until the boss dies.
After the boss: back to the hub

The wiki does not describe how to leave the {creature:Goshnar's Hatred} room or the way back to the hub. Go back the way you came; if there is no passage, a {item:Temple Teleport Scroll} sends you to your city's temple (it does not work in No-Logout zones or with a Logout Block or Protection Zone Block), and return to the hub via the route in section 2. With the five access bosses dead, head for the final boss: the portal to the **south-west** of the hub (section 14).

**Recommended protection:** Physical (with Stone Skin Amulets, especially the Knight), Death (Dreadful Harvesters and white tiles), Energy (the constant phantasmal damage) and Fire (fire explosions). **Elements to use:** Death for single-target attacks on the boss and the Aspects; Fire for area (the {item:Great Fireball Rune|Great Fireball Runes} are the preferred area rune, but all the mages' waves count). The fight combines many mechanics from the previous bosses.

After killing the five access bosses in this round, enter the portal to the **south-west** of the main hub. Team of up to 5 players; you have at most 20 minutes and the boss has a **68-hour** cooldown.
The 5th taint is applied in this room: nobody can keep a large mana reserve. Expect it and do not panic when your mana drops quickly.
{creature:Goshnar's Megalomania} alternates between three forms during the fight:
Immune to all damage. This is how the fight starts.
It is charging the Annihilation attack, but is still vulnerable.

While the boss is invulnerable, you have to kill **4 {creature:Aspect of Power|Aspects of Power}** to make it vulnerable. Killing an Aspect while the boss is already vulnerable **does not count** towards the next round.

There is an invisible counter, Goshnar's **Madness**, which makes the boss stronger: the higher it is, the less damage Megalomania takes. It rises slowly over time and can go up or down depending on the following mechanics.

During the fight {creature:Lesser Splinter of Madness|Lesser Splinters of Madness} appear, which over time become {creature:Greater Splinter of Madness|Greater} and then {creature:Mighty Splinter of Madness|Mighty Splinters of Madness}. To get rid of them, make them walk over the body of an Aspect of Power ({item:Phantasmal Ooze}): when they step on it they turn into {item:Cleansed Sanity}, which you have to use on the {item:Maw (Object)|Maw}, to the **south** of the room (as with Goshnar's Cruelty). If a Mighty Splinter is not removed in time, the boss absorbs it and the Madness goes up.
If there is more than one Splinter in the room, deal first with the one in the strongest form.

Two {creature:Necromantic Focus|Necromantic Focuses} keep appearing, to the **west** and **east** of the room. When killed they leave {item:Necromantic Remains} on the ground; stepping on them reduces the Madness (*Your soul is weakened by the destruction of the remains but the intensity of madness is lessened!*). If nobody steps on them, the boss absorbs them and gets stronger.

As with Goshnar's Hatred, but slower: the counter next to your name goes up every 10 seconds, with several warning messages, up to **36**. From then on *The dread's torment is now lethal!* appears every 10 seconds and you take up to 5 600 death damage each time (about 700 with an {item:Stone Skin Amulet|SSA}, a {item:Might Ring} and {wiki:Powerful Lich Shroud|Powerful Lich Shroud} imbuements). To reset the counter, step on a {item:Phantasmal Ooze} (*The ooze calms your dread but leaves you vulnerable to phantasmal attacks!*): for a few seconds you are more vulnerable to phantasmal damage. Since the Oozes are also needed for the Splinters, use them wisely, or only when the counter is already really high.

The boss's ghost wave deals *Phantasmal Damage*, which is actually Life Drain. Normally it is low (*You took minor phantasmal damage.*), but if you stepped on a Phantasmal Ooze recently you take **huge** damage (as with Goshnar's Spite). In addition, every 30 seconds *You emit painful energies!* appears and each character casts an exori-like energy spell that deals Life Drain to the **other** players caught in it (not to the caster): do not stand next to each other.

A random player is transformed into a {creature:Massive Fire Elemental} and explodes in a large area 6 seconds later. Shortly after the boss shouts *FEEL THE POWER OF MY WRATH!!* white tiles appear on the floor: they destroy any Necromantic Remains on them and, **8 seconds** later, deal **10 000** death damage to anyone **not** standing on them. This only happens 2 or 3 times per fight: decide beforehand who steps on the tiles and who tanks the damage with Stone Skin, Might Ring and other death protection.
Transformation into a Massive Fire Elemental

Only once in the fight, Megalomania switches to its **blue** form, gets stuck in place and shouts *ENOUGH! I WILL MAKE YOU SUFFER FOR YOUR INSOLENCE!* and *NOW - I - WILL - ANNIHILATE - YOU!*. Everyone runs away from the boss to avoid the spell, but keeps attacking it: this phase lasts about 7 seconds. The boss can also put Fear on its target.

While the boss is invulnerable, focus on the **Aspects of Power**. As with the other bosses, controlling the number of Dreadful Harvesters is crucial: the shooters avoid hitting them and use single-target attacks on the Aspects, to reduce the chance of more appearing (2nd taint). Only use area attacks when there are several Harvesters in the room, or when you can hit them, the boss and the Aspects at the same time. When the Aspects die, lure the Splinters onto their bodies.
Strategy: Necromantic Focus and resetting the Dread

If necessary, you can ignore the Necromantic Focuses completely. But when there are no Aspects alive and the boss is still invulnerable, the shooters can attack those pillars for the small boosts they give; go back to the Aspects as soon as they appear, because they are the only way to make the boss vulnerable. When an Aspect dies **without** any Splinter in the room, that is the moment for a player to step on the Phantasmal Ooze to reset the Dread. Agree on the order beforehand and do not let several players get close to 36 at the same time: they would use up several Oozes and greatly delay the Splinters.

After each round of 4 Aspects, the boss is vulnerable for **70 seconds**: deal as much damage to it as possible (if you need to, use strong area attacks to also hit the Harvesters and the Aspects). The Aspects keep appearing in this phase: you can leave them on low health so they count towards the next round, but not killing them affects the Splinters and makes the boss stronger. The recommended approach is to keep killing the Aspects and doing the Splinters even while the boss is vulnerable.

The boss switches to the blue form when its health gets a little above yellow. Strong teams use the {wiki:Avatar|Avatar} spells the first time the boss turns green, to make it go blue in a single round of Aspects. Weaker teams need more rounds. Watch out: the blue form immediately ends the green form, so if the boss turns blue shortly after turning green, that round of Aspects is "wasted" and the fight drags on.

Repeat the cycle throughout the fight: Aspects of Power, Splinters and damage on the vulnerable boss are the main focus; the remaining mechanics are done when possible. When the boss dies, your taints disappear (section 3).
End of the fight: taints cleared and boss loot (see section 15)

After killing the final boss, go back to the hub and say {key:hi} and {key:task} to the {npc:Flickering Soul}. You receive the {wiki:Revenant Outfits|Revenant} outfit and the quest is complete. The wiki does not describe how to leave the {creature:Goshnar's Megalomania} room: go back the way you came; if you have to use a {item:Temple Teleport Scroll}, return to the hub via the route in section 2.

Enter the portal **behind a {npc:Flickering Soul}**, in the main hall, and open the {item:Brass-Shod Chest} on the **north** side. The chest gives **one random item** from the {wiki:Soul Set} to each character, only once. The Soul Set pieces require level 400 to be used.
In the same room as the chest there is a {wiki:Magic Forcefield}: enter it and you are sent to the **Thais depot**.

The secret achievement **Soul Mender** is obtained by killing {creature:Goshnar's Malice}, {creature:Goshnar's Hatred}, {creature:Goshnar's Spite}, {creature:Goshnar's Cruelty} and {creature:Goshnar's Greed} **while having all 5 Goshnar's Taints**. You only have the 5 taints after killing the five bosses, so you have to kill them again (respecting the 20-hour cooldowns) **before** {creature:Goshnar's Megalomania}, which clears your taints.

All the bosses drop {item:Crystal Coin|Crystal Coins}, gems and giant gems and lots of potions (Supreme Health, Ultimate Mana and Ultimate Spirit, Mastermind, Berserk, Bullseye and Transcendence). The most interesting items:
{item:Megalomania's Skull}, {item:Megalomania's Essence}, {item:Figurine of Megalomania} (and the figurines of the other five), {item:Dragon Figurine}, {item:Bag You Desire}

The {item:Bag You Desire} turns into a random piece of the Soul Set when you open the Reward Container it drops in. Putting the Soul War bosses in the Bosstiary boss slot increases your chance of looting it.
Revenant addons and Phantasmal Jade mount

With the base outfit, do the {wiki:Revenant Outfits Quest}: use a {item:The Skull of a Beast} for the 1st addon (*Now the beast is unleashed!*) and a {item:Bracelet of Strengthening} for the 2nd (*Wild power flows though your body!*); with both you get the achievement **Unleash the Beast**. After completing the quest, you can also get the {wiki:Phantasmal Jade} mount by using 4 {item:Spectral Horseshoe|Spectral Horseshoes}, a {item:Spectral Horse Tack} and a {item:Spectral Saddle} (achievement **You Got Horse Power**).

The bosses can be repeated for loot: the access bosses every 20 hours and {creature:Goshnar's Megalomania} every 68 hours. Remember: for each Megalomania you have to kill the five access bosses again (and repeat the zone accesses).
The taints only work inside the Soul War zones (including the boss rooms); outside them they do not affect you.
If you fail the final boss you lose the last two taints and the progress of two random bosses; say {key:shards} to the {npc:Flickering Soul} to find out which ones you have to repeat.

In the Furious Crater you can also reach the bottom floor with {spell:Levitate} at {coord:33841,31867,6}; on that floor there are creatures and a chest in the west corridor ({coord:33810,31868,7}) that can give, for example, 3 {item:Gold Ingot|Gold Ingots}, a {item:White Gem}, a {item:Diabolic Skull}, a {item:Unicorn Figurine} or a {item:Bar of Gold}.
The five Soul War zones are among the hardest hunting zones in the game (level 600 recommended). Ebb and Flow is especially dangerous because of the Fear and the holes with no way back.
